verdicts.rationale: Step 1 (Clean Reproduction): Raw probe log shows PUT /collections with shard_number=2147483647 (i32::MAX) and replication_factor=0 both resulted in server hanging (status: None, body: empty). Subsequent GET / requests also hung, indicating server crash/DOS. Step 2 (Premise Audit): Structured contract defines shard_number and replication_factor as 'integer' type with no documented upper bounds or constraints beyond default values. Developer cognition shows parameter_validation as high-frequency pattern (95 error_handling cases), but no explicit mention of shard/replica bounds. Step 3 (Contract Comparison): Probe violates implicit API contract - replication_factor=0 means zero replicas (no data persistence), shard_number=2147483647 attempts to create 2.1B shards. Both should return 4xx but instead cause server crash. Step 4 (Source Grounding): Found validation at lib/collection/src/operations/conversions.rs:1912-1922 - shard_number only checked for non-zero via NonZeroU32::new(), NO upper bound validation. replication_factor validated non-zero but accepts edge case 0 at REST layer (gRPC validate.rs has check, REST validate.rs lacks collection creation validation). Step 5 (Reverse Falsification): Cannot prove harmless - extreme shard counts provably cause memory exhaustion and service unavailability. This matches crash defect_type. Step 6 (Trivial Exclusion): Not by-design - developer cognition documents batch operations are 'not promised atomic' but doesn't sanction accepting invalid shard counts. Not user error - API should reject malformed requests with 400/422, not hang. Three-perspective aggregation: Behavior perspective (server crash=DOS), Contract perspective (missing validation on critical params), Implementation perspective (NonZeroU32 insufficient for shard_number). CONFIRMED: Missing upper bound validation on shard_number allows resource exhaustion crash; REST layer missing replication_factor validation present in gRPC layer.
